events.message:
TELCO-6117 — Modernise the "Contact us" flow
Priority: Medium Component: Customer Experience

Description

The current "Contact us" flow is dated and results in poor NPS scores in post-interaction surveys. Modernise it to align with our new digital strategy and reduce time-to-resolution.

Acceptance Criteria

The new flow feels modern and responsive.
Wait times are reduced.
Accessibility is improved.
The design is consistent with our new brand.
Customers can seamlessly hand off to a human agent when needed.
Non-Functional

Scale must support peak load.
Personal information must be handled appropriately.

input.brief:
TELCO-6117 — Modernise the "Contact us" flow
Priority: Medium
Component: Customer Experience

Description
The current "Contact us" flow is dated and results in poor NPS scores in post-interaction surveys. Modernise it to align with our new digital strategy and reduce time-to-resolution.

Acceptance Criteria
1. The new flow feels modern and responsive.
2. Wait times are reduced.
3. Accessibility is improved.
4. The design is consistent with our new brand.
5. Customers can seamlessly hand off to a human agent when needed.

Non-Functional
6. Scale must support peak load.
7. Personal information must be handled appropriately.

result.summary_one_paragraph: TELCO-6117 proposes modernising the existing "Contact us" flow to align it with the new digital strategy, improve post-interaction NPS, and reduce time-to-resolution. The stated outcomes cover a modern and responsive experience, reduced wait times, improved accessibility, consistency with the new brand, and handoff to a human agent when needed, alongside peak-load scalability and appropriate handling of personal information.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The new Contact us flow is modern and responsive.
The design is consistent with the new brand.
Customers can hand off seamlessly to a human agent when needed.

ambiguities.text: “Modern and responsive” has no defined user-experience criteria, supported devices, viewport expectations, or measurable response-time target.
“Wait times are reduced” does not define the current baseline, the wait-time measure, target reduction, customer segment, or measurement period.
“Accessibility is improved” does not identify an accessibility standard, conformance level, supported assistive technologies, or verification method.
“Consistent with our new brand” does not identify the applicable brand guidelines or design-system version.
“Seamlessly hand off” and “when needed” do not define handoff triggers, customer actions, agent availability behaviour, context transfer, or success criteria.
“Peak load” does not define expected concurrency, transaction volume, traffic profile, service-level targets, or load-test conditions.
“Handled appropriately” does not define applicable privacy obligations, permitted data, consent requirements, retention, access controls, or data-sharing rules.

missing_NFRs: Browser, device, and assistive-technology compatibility requirements
unstated_assumptions: A human-agent service exists and is capable of receiving customer handoffs.
Wait time and time-to-resolution can be measured before and after the change.
A current brand guideline or design system is available for implementation and review.
A defined peak-load profile can be obtained for capacity validation.
The flow may collect or process personal information.
testability_issues: No acceptance criterion provides measurable pass/fail thresholds.
No baseline or target is specified for wait-time reduction or time-to-resolution.
No accessibility standard or conformance level is specified.
No brand artefacts or approval criteria are identified.
No definition exists for a successful human-agent handoff, including the information that must be transferred.
No peak-load volume, concurrency level, or performance service level is specified.
No policy, regulation, or controls define what appropriate personal-information handling means.

risk_areas.reason: The handoff trigger, agent-availability behaviour, and definition of seamless transfer are unspecified.
The requirement identifies personal information but provides no applicable privacy, consent, retention, or access-control rules.
Peak demand is required to be supported, but no workload profile or capacity target is provided.
Improvement is required without an accessibility standard or validation approach.
The stated NPS, wait-time, and resolution-time goals cannot be verified without baselines, targets, and measurement definitions.

suggested_questions: What measurable wait-time target is required, and what baseline and reporting period should be used?
How is time-to-resolution defined, measured, and targeted for this flow?
Which accessibility standard and conformance level must the new flow meet?
Which new-brand guidelines, design system, or approved reference designs must be used?
What events indicate that a customer needs a human agent?
How should the flow behave when no human agent is available, and what customer context must be transferred during handoff?
What peak-load volumes, concurrency levels, traffic patterns, and response-time targets must be supported?
Which personal information may be collected or transferred, and which privacy, consent, retention, and security requirements apply?
Which channels, devices, browsers, and assistive technologies are in scope for the Contact us flow?
What NPS outcome or improvement target is expected, and how will it be attributed to this change?
cause_effect_hints: Current dated Contact us flow -> poor post-interaction NPS
Modernised flow -> alignment with new digital strategy
edge_case_hints: Human agent is unavailable when a handoff is needed
Peak-load conditions occur during the Contact us flow
Personal information is entered or transferred during a handoff

scenarios_in.name: Explore the Contact us flow for modern responsive interaction
scenarios_in.given: the new Contact us flow is available in the agreed test environment
scenarios_in.when: a tester explores its layout, interaction feedback, and viewport changes across the TBD supported browser and device scope
scenarios_in.then: the observations are recorded for review against the TBD modern-and-responsive experience criteria without asserting an unspecified threshold

scenarios_in.name: Measure wait time against the TBD baseline and target
scenarios_in.given: a current-flow baseline and a new-flow measurement dataset can be collected
scenarios_in.when: wait-time measurements are captured for the TBD population and TBD observation window using the same defined measure
scenarios_in.then: the comparative results are retained for assessment against the TBD reduction target

scenarios_in.name: Explore keyboard and assistive-technology access to the Contact us flow
scenarios_in.given: the new Contact us flow is available with keyboard and assistive technology
scenarios_in.when: a tester navigates, reads, operates, corrects, and completes the flow using the TBD accessibility standard and assistive-technology matrix
scenarios_in.then: accessibility observations and defects are recorded for assessment against the TBD conformance requirement

scenarios_in.name: Review the Contact us flow against the TBD brand reference
scenarios_in.given: the rendered Contact us flow and the applicable brand or design-system reference are available
scenarios_in.when: a reviewer compares visual and interaction elements with the TBD authoritative brand reference
scenarios_in.then: conformances and deviations are documented for approval by the TBD brand owner

scenarios_in.name: Explore customer-requested and system-needed human-agent handoff paths
scenarios_in.given: a customer is progressing through the Contact us flow and the human-agent service is available
scenarios_in.when: the customer requests an agent or a TBD handoff condition occurs
scenarios_in.then: the handoff behaviour, customer context transfer, and outcome are captured for assessment against the TBD handoff rules

scenarios_in.name: Characterise Contact us flow behaviour under the TBD peak workload
scenarios_in.given: a performance environment and monitoring are available
scenarios_in.when: the flow is exercised using the TBD peak-load traffic profile and concurrency level
scenarios_in.then: throughput, response time, errors, and resource observations are retained for assessment against TBD service targets

scenarios_in.name: Review personal-information handling across the Contact us flow
scenarios_in.given: the data fields, integrations, logs, storage locations, and agent-handoff path can be inspected
scenarios_in.when: a reviewer traces personal information through collection, display, transfer, logging, storage, and access activities
scenarios_in.then: the observed data flows and controls are documented for assessment against the TBD privacy and security policy
